software.name: AIPrompt
software.shortDescription: AI prompt generator, library, and assembler for Windows — with a built-in ROADMAP.md file generator.
software.description: AIPrompt is a Windows desktop app for building, organizing, and assembling prompts for generative AI (text, code, image, and more). Pull terms and phrases from a local library, organized by type and category, to quickly assemble a coherent prompt, then export it as Markdown or plain text. It also includes a dedicated generator for structured ROADMAP.md files for other projects. The app is organized into eight sections reachable from the main navigation rail: Dashboard, Term library, Prompt assembler, Saved prompts, ROADMAP.md generator, Import/Export, Settings, and About.

notes: First stable release of AIPrompt: a Windows desktop app to build, organize, and assemble AI prompts from a local library of reusable terms and phrases, and to generate structured `ROADMAP.md` files.
## Installation

Download `AIPromptSetup_x64.exe` below, run it (no administrator rights required), and launch AIPrompt from the Start Menu or Desktop shortcut. Windows 10/11 x64, self-contained (.NET 8) — no separate runtime install needed.
## Highlights since the last pre-release
### Added

Automatic semantic versioning: a single `VERSION` file drives `Version`/`AssemblyVersion`/`FileVersion`/`InformationalVersion` across all projects, with a local build script (`scripts/build.ps1`) that auto-increments `PATCH`
Windows installer built with Inno Setup 6 (per-user install, Start Menu / Desktop shortcuts, clean uninstall) and a one-step build script (`scripts/build-installer.ps1`)
Final `README.md` with installation instructions and real application screenshots
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, issue templates, and `CODEOWNERS`
### Changed
About tab now shows the full informational version (including pre-release suffixes) instead of a truncated 3-part version
### Fixed
Removed a stray AI co-author mention found in git history during the final compliance pass (history rewritten, affected tags recreated)
See `CHANGELOG.md` for the complete history.

the `README.md`.

information reviewed and brought up to date.

technique (dead code elimination, declaration merging, loop golfing,

renaming, operator simplification), unit tests for every de-golfing
technique (conditional expansion, loop expansion, operator expansion,

session history store, and the JS/WASM engine bridge, and interface

build, checking that every emitted asset reference is relative.

deployment workflow.

now loaded on demand via dynamic `import()` instead of being bundled
into the application's initial entry chunk.

(Three.js, CodeMirror, the AST/golfing engine) instead of a single
monolithic bundle, reducing the initial entry chunk from roughly
1 MB to about 36 kB and removing the Vite large-chunk warning.

`Alt+G` toggles Golf / De-golf, `Alt+M` toggles Minified / Justified,
`Alt+C` copies the converted code, `Alt+E` opens Export, `Alt+H`
opens History, `Alt+B` opens Benchmark, `Alt+R` opens Rules, `Alt+I`
opens Import, and `Escape` closes any open panel. Every corresponding
button now shows its shortcut in a tooltip.
Keyboard-visible focus outline applied consistently across every
interactive element, and `aria-expanded` / `aria-haspopup` states
kept in sync on all dropdown-style panels for assistive technology.
Reactive Three.js background transition: the point-field background
now animates a brief pulse (speed, size, and opacity) on every
conversion, and respects the operating system's reduced-motion
preference by disabling the animation entirely when requested.
### Changed
Refined responsive breakpoints for tablet and mobile viewports: the
header and its controls now wrap cleanly, dropdown panels
(History, Benchmark, Export, Rules) constrain themselves to the
viewport width instead of overflowing on narrow screens, and the
status bar and header actions reflow on small screens.
### Added
Local file import: drag and drop a `.js` or `.txt` file onto the
original editor panel, or use the new "Import" button to pick a file,
to load its content for conversion.
Export of the converted code as a downloadable `.js` or `.txt` file
from the new "Export" menu in the converted panel.
One-click "Copy" button to copy the converted code to the clipboard,
with transient confirmation feedback.
Session-local conversion history: every distinct edit to the original
code is recorded (debounced) with its timestamp, direction, and
compression ratio, browsable from the new "History" panel and
restorable with a single click. The history is kept in memory only
and is cleared on page reload.
Undo / Redo controls for the original editor, exposed both as header
buttons and through the existing keyboard shortcuts.
### Added
Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly, providing a high-performance
implementation of the whitespace-compaction pass and lexical token
counting used by the minified output and status bar.
Transparent engine bridge: the application attempts to load the
compiled WASM engine on startup and automatically falls back to the
existing JavaScript implementation when the WASM module has not been
built or fails to load, with no change in behavior or output for the
end user.
"Engine" badge in the header indicating whether the active engine is
WASM or the JS fallback.
Integrated performance benchmark panel comparing the JS and WASM
engines on the current source across a fixed number of iterations,
with per-task timing bars and a computed speedup factor.
`npm run build:wasm` script compiling the Rust engine with
`wasm-pack`, wired into the production build and into the GitHub
Actions deployment workflow.
### Added
Reverse conversion (de-golfing): golfed code can now be converted back
into structured, readable code.
Restoration of readable variable names: identifiers are renamed
according to their role (function names, parameters, loop counters,
general values) instead of the original single-letter golfed names.
Restoration of indentation and block structure: single-statement
bodies are re-wrapped in blocks and the result is reformatted with
clean indentation.
Heuristic reconstruction of common golfed patterns: ternary and
`&&`-shortcut conditionals are expanded back into `if`/`else`
statements, countdown `for` loops are expanded back into ascending
loops, and double-negation / falsy-literal boolean shortcuts are
expanded back into their explicit form.
Functional equivalence validation: after de-golfing, the reconstructed
code is re-golfed and compared against a canonical signature of the
original input to confirm the conversion is behavior-preserving, shown
as an "Equivalence" status badge.
Direction toggle in the interface to switch between "Golf" (structured
to golfed) and "De-golf" (golfed to structured) conversion.
### Added
Advanced loop golfing: counting `for` loops are rewritten as reverse
countdown loops when the loop variable is unused in the body and the
bound is safe to evaluate once, shortening the loop header.
Ternary and conditional golfing: `if`/`else` statements are rewritten
as conditional (ternary) expressions for matching `return` statements
and matching assignments, and single-branch `if` statements using an
expression are rewritten with the `&&` short-circuit shortcut.
Native call golfing: known JavaScript golfing shortcuts are applied
automatically, including `Boolean(x)` to `!!x`, `indexOf` presence
checks to `includes`, `Array.prototype` to `[]`, and `.apply(null, x)`
calls to spread syntax.
Configurable golfing rules panel: each golfing technique (dead code
elimination, declaration merging, loop golfing, ternary golfing,
native call golfing, variable renaming, operator simplification) can
be toggled on or off independently, with the converted output
updating immediately.
Character count display for both the original and converted code.
Compression score, shown as a percentage of characters saved by the
conversion.
### Added
Golfing conversion pipeline applied to every conversion: minification,
variable renaming, operator simplification, declaration merging, and
dead code elimination.
Minification engine: strips whitespace, newlines, and redundant
semicolons from the converted output.
Scope-aware variable renaming engine, assigning short identifiers
(`a`, `b`, `c`, ...) while avoiding collisions with global references
and reserved words.
Operator simplification engine: converts increment/decrement patterns
and compound arithmetic assignments to their shorter forms, and
boolean literals to their shortest equivalent.
Automatic merging of adjacent variable declarations of the same kind.
Dead code elimination: removes unreachable statements, redundant pure
expression statements, and literal `if` branches.
Toggle button to switch the converted panel between "Minified" and
"Justified" output modes.
"Justified" mode: readable reformatting of the converted code with
clean indentation.
### Added
Dual-pane code editor built on CodeMirror 6 (Original / Converted).
White theme applied to the code editors, matching the interface.
Real-time synchronization: edits in the original pane automatically
update the converted pane.
Automatic source language detection, with JavaScript as the priority
language.
Source code tokenization and AST parsing powered by Acorn.
Status bar showing detected language, token count, and character count.
### Added
Initial project foundation with Vite and TypeScript.
GitHub Pages compatible build configuration.
Three.js background scene integrated into the interface.
White theme baseline styling.
Rust and WebAssembly engine skeleton for the future conversion engine.
Initial `ConversionEngine` core module.
Continuous deployment workflow to GitHub Pages.

App: a "Perf HUD" viewport toggle overlays eval/frame time and keyframe count live; the Diagnostics panel shows the per-track cost table, a rolling frame-time graph, and "Export Session Log (CSV)". Note: there's no separately measurable "GPU frame time" in this architecture — the 3D viewport is CPU-painter-drawn, not a real wgpu render pass — so only CPU-side timings are reported, documented as such rather than fabricated

- **14.2 Shader Complexity Analysis:** `estimate_instruction_count` is a documented text-level heuristic (statement/operator/call counts), not a real compiler-verified instruction count; `platform_tier_report` checks it against rough guideline thresholds for Mobile/Integrated-GPU/Desktop. `detect_optimization_suggestions` finds constant-folding no-ops (`* 1.0`, `+ 0.0`, …) and always-true/always-false `if` branches (with real brace-matching for safely removing dead `if (false)` blocks); `apply_with_diff` performs the byte-range replacements and returns a before/after preview for the one-click "Apply Suggested Optimizations" action. New module `glsl-codegen/src/analysis/` (`complexity.rs`, `suggestions.rs`)

- **14.3 Curve Simplification & LOD:** `simplify_curve` runs an iterative (non-recursive, stack-overflow-safe) Douglas-Peucker pass over each keyframe's `(time, value)` or `(time, x, y, z)` point, preserving both timing and shape within a tolerance — exact when kept segments are evaluated with linear interpolation, documented as approximate for curved interpolation modes between kept keyframes. `LodPreset` (Desktop/Integrated GPU/Mobile) wraps built-in tolerance presets. New module `core-engine/src/curve_simplify.rs`. App: tolerance slider + live preview + per-preset buttons in the Diagnostics panel, applied to the selected curve via undo-tracked `FullSnapshot`

- **14.4 Memory & Stability Profiling:** new optional `heap-profiling` Cargo feature (mirrors the existing `puffin-profiling` pattern) wires `dhat` as the global allocator and writes `dhat-heap.json` for offline inspection with the dhat viewer — opt-in, adds nothing to a normal build. A panic hook (`app/src/crash_report.rs`) writes a local, never-transmitted crash report (timestamp, panic location/message, backtrace) to the app data directory; the Diagnostics panel lists captured reports. `generate_stress_test_project` builds a synthetic multi-track, multi-thousand-keyframe timeline for stability testing, exposed both as a core-engine test fixture (asserts a 10k-keyframe evaluation pass completes without panicking within budget) and as a "Generate Stress-Test Project" Diagnostics panel action
- New module `core-engine/src/diagnostics/` (`performance.rs`, `stress_test.rs`). App: new "Diagnostics" panel bringing all of the above together
- Tests: 8 new performance/stress-test unit tests, 7 curve-simplification tests, 12 shader-analysis tests

**Phase 4.3 — Tangent handle gizmos & multi-keyframe group manipulation:** the 3D viewport's translation gizmo now actually works — fixed a pre-existing bug where the picked axis was never stored, making the drag code unreachable. `ViewportState::active_gizmo_handle: Option<GizmoHandle>` is now set by hit-testing on drag-start (`Position(axis)`, `Group(axis)`, `InTangent`, `OutTangent`) and cleared on drag-stop. Selecting a single `Vec3`/`CubicBezier` keyframe now shows its incoming/outgoing tangent handles as small diamonds with a connector line, freely draggable in the camera's yaw-relative plane; selecting multiple keyframes shows one group gizmo at their centroid that moves them all together, preserving relative offsets. New `Command::MoveTangent` undo entry for tangent edits.
### Changed

**Native file picker replaces typed-path dialogs:** Open/Save Project, audio import, BVH mocap import, and asset-library trajectory-template export/import now use a real native Windows file dialog (`rfd`) instead of a text field the user had to type a path into by hand. This supersedes the earlier "simple path-entry dialog pattern" (documented in the Phase 3.5 status note above) that was originally chosen specifically to avoid adding a file-dialog dependency; `rfd` is a native OS-dialog wrapper with no network calls, so it doesn't conflict with the offline-first requirement. `ProjectPathDialog`/`ProjectDialogMode`/`AudioImportDialog` and their `path_buf` fields are removed from `AppState` in favor of a plain `Option<String>` error per feature, shown in a small dismissible window only on failure — the OS dialog itself already handles browsing/cancel/filename entry, so a custom modal for the happy path is no longer needed. New dependency: `rfd` (app crate only).
### Added
**Phase 12 — Non-Linear Timeline, Layers & Version History:**

- **12.1 Timeline Layers:** `LayerStack`/`TimelineLayer` — stacked, named layers (`Base`/`Override`/`Additive` blend modes, per-layer opacity, solo/mute/lock) composited by matching track name across layers; `evaluate_track` blends (lerp for Base/Override, sum for Additive) scalar/position/rotation curve values; `merge_down` flattens a layer into the one beneath it, baking a resampled blend for `Base`/`Additive` or keeping an `Override` layer's curves verbatim, while tracks unique to either side pass through untouched. Additive to the existing single-`tracks` timeline model — projects that never touch layers are unaffected

- **12.2 Nested Sequences:** `SubSequence`/`SubSequenceInstance`/`SubSequenceRegistry` — reusable named track bundles placed as time-remapped instances (start offset, speed, optional loop) either on the master timeline or nested inside another sub-sequence; `validate_no_circular_nesting` DFS-detects both direct self-reference and indirect cycles through multiple sequences, and `add_nested_instance` rejects (and rolls back) any addition that would create one

- **12.3 Variants (A/B Takes):** `VariantStore`/`TimelineVariant` — full named snapshots of the current tracks kept alongside the master, non-destructively; `diff_tracks` compares two track lists by matching tracks on name and keyframes on id (added/removed/modified), shared by both variant-vs-master and snapshot-vs-snapshot diffing; `merge_keyframes_from_variant` selectively promotes individual keyframes from a variant into master

- **12.4 Version History & Annotations:** `SnapshotManager` — filesystem-backed, offline history of full `.stcp` project snapshots with a JSON index; `restore_with_backup` always snapshots the current project first, so restoring can never silently discard unsaved work; `diff_snapshots` reuses the 12.3 diff algorithm; `MarkerTrack`/`TimelineMarker` — free-text annotations pinned to time positions, kept time-sorted, with radius-based lookup

- New module `core-engine/src/sequencing/` (`layers.rs`, `subsequence.rs`, `variant.rs`, `version_history.rs`, `marker.rs`), re-exported from the crate root. `TimelineState` gains `layer_stack`, `sub_sequences`, `variants`, `markers` fields (all serde-default, non-breaking)

- App: new "Layers / Sequences / Variants / History" panel — layer stack editor (add/reorder/blend-mode/opacity/solo/mute/lock/duplicate/merge-down), sub-sequence manager with drill-in/drill-out navigation (temporarily swaps the Timeline/Curve Editor panels onto the sub-sequence's own tracks, with an explicit save-or-discard on drill-out) and root/nested instance placement, variant creation/diff/apply/selective-merge, and snapshot creation/diff/restore-with-confirmation plus marker add/remove/jump-to-time

- Note: layer composition (`evaluate_track`) and sub-sequence instance time-remapping are engine-level capabilities with app-side editing UI, but are not yet wired into the live camera/GLSL evaluation pipeline that drives the 3D viewport, preview, and export — that integration is a natural follow-up, not part of this change

- Tests: 37 new unit tests across the five new modules (blend composition incl. solo/mute, merge-down for all three blend modes, time remap incl. looping, self/indirect cycle rejection with rollback, diff add/remove/modify detection, selective merge, snapshot create/load/persist-across-reload/restore-with-backup/delete, marker sort/lookup)
**Phase 13.2 — Asset & Preset Library:**

- `AssetLibrary`: local, flat store of `CurvePreset` (single tagged/categorized `Curve`) and `TrajectoryTemplate` (tagged/categorized set of `Track`s) entries, with case-insensitive name/category/tag search, per-entry favoriting, and a deduplicated MRU "recently used" list

- Shareable fragment export/import: `save_template_fragment` / `load_template_fragment` write a single `TrajectoryTemplate` to its own `.stcp` fragment file (a `fragment_kind`-discriminated JSON document, distinct from a full `Project` file) for sharing between projects

- Thumbnail generation reuses the existing offline CPU frame renderer from the Phase 8 export pipeline (`render_frame_rgba8`) rather than introducing a second render path: a curve preset is wired in as a synthetic camera-position track, a template renders its own tracks directly, both sampled at the mid-duration point and encoded to PNG bytes via the existing `write_png_rgba8`
- New module `core-engine/src/library/` (`preset.rs`, `fragment_io.rs`, `thumbnail.rs`), re-exported from the crate root

- App: "Asset Library" panel — search, per-entry thumbnail + favorite/apply/delete, save the selected curve as a preset or the selected track as a template, export/import template fragments, favorites & recently-used quick-access strip. Library persists to `asset_library.json` in the app data directory, independent of any single project
- Tests: `AssetLibrary` CRUD/search/favorites/MRU/round-trip, fragment save/load and rejection of non-fragment files, thumbnail pixel-buffer sizing and PNG signature
**Phase 10.3 — Motion Capture Import:**

- Dependency-free recursive-descent BVH (Biovision Hierarchy) parser: `HIERARCHY` skeleton (joint offsets, per-joint channel layout, `End Site` leaves) and `MOTION` per-frame channel data, local-file-only (offline-first)

- Forward-kinematics retargeting (`retarget_to_camera_path`): evaluates world-space position/rotation of a chosen joint per frame (root or any end effector) via a single forward pass over the parent-before-child joint order
- `MocapSmoothingFilter`: centered moving-average noise reduction with a configurable window radius, applied to both position and (hemisphere-corrected) rotation
- Non-destructive preview → user-approved bake flow: `bake_mocap_position_to_curve` / `bake_mocap_rotation_to_curve` insert keyframes only once the retargeted+filtered trajectory is committed
- New module `core-engine/src/mocap/` (`bvh.rs`, `retarget.rs`, `filter.rs`), re-exported from the crate root
- App: "Physics & Mocap" panel — BVH file load, joint picker, scale/offset/smoothing controls, retarget preview, bake to the selected curve

- Tests: BVH parser tests against a fixture file (`core-engine/tests/fixtures/simple_arm.bvh`), FK retargeting tests (root position channel, parent offset composition, scale/offset), smoothing filter tests, bake tests
**Phase 10.2 — Rigid-Body & Collision Awareness:**

- `RigidBodySolver`: mass/stiffness/damping spring-damper integrator (semi-implicit Euler, unconditionally stable) for camera spring/inertia behavior, with a `critical_damping` helper and optional max-speed clamp
- `ObstacleVolume` (sphere/box) + `ObstacleSet`: user-defined keep-out volumes with a configurable clearance margin and signed-distance queries

- `preview_collision_avoidance`: non-destructive per-sample suggestion that pushes path positions penetrating an obstacle's margin-inflated surface back outside it; `bake_collision_avoidance` commits an approved preview into curve keyframes
- `min_distance_diagnostic`: samples a curve's clearance to the nearest obstacle over time, for a diagnostic graph overlay
- New module `core-engine/src/camera/physics.rs` and `core-engine/src/camera/collision.rs`, re-exported from `camera` and the crate root
- App: "Physics & Mocap" panel — rigid-body spring preview (settle/overshoot readout), obstacle list editor, collision-avoidance preview + bake, min-clearance readout
- `TimelineState` gains `obstacles: ObstacleSet` (serde-default, non-breaking)

- Tests: unit tests in `physics.rs` (critical/underdamped settle behavior, max-speed clamp, zero-dt no-op) and `collision.rs` (signed distance for both shapes, avoidance preview, bake, diagnostic, margin)
**Phase 10.1 — Path Constraint Solver:**
- `FollowSplineConstraint`: locks camera position to any position `Curve`, with either a world-space offset or a path-relative (right/up/forward) offset that stays consistent as the path turns
- `BankingSolver`: auto-roll angle derived from the path's local curvature (`|v x a| / |v|^3`, finite-difference), signed by turn direction and clamped to a configurable max roll
- `LookAheadSolver`: samples the path ahead of the current time for predictive orientation aiming, holding at the curve's end instead of extrapolating past it

- `ArcLengthTable` + `SpeedNormalizationSolver`: builds an arc-length lookup table (binary-search distance→time) so playback along arbitrarily/unevenly keyframed curves can be reparameterized to constant velocity
- New module `core-engine/src/camera/path_constraint.rs`, re-exported from `camera` and the crate root
- Tests: unit tests in `path_constraint.rs` (straight line, quarter-circle curvature, arc-length round-trip, constant-speed remap)
### Fixed

**Position-curve Catmull-Rom evaluation bug:** `evaluate()` was returning `Value::Scalar(0.0)` for any `Vec3` (position) curve using a Catmull-Rom interpolation mode — the mode `Keyframe::new_position` uses by default — instead of interpolating `position_value` component-wise. This silently froze default-created position curves in place. Fixed by dispatching Catmull-Rom evaluation on `channel_type`, the same way the existing `CubicBezier` branch already does. Regression tests added in `core-engine/tests/catmull_rom_position_regression.rs`.
**Phase 9 — Multi-Camera Rig, Switching & Compositing System:**
- `CameraRig` data model with parent/child hierarchy, mute/active flags, color tags, auto-bank, shared look-at binding
- Non-breaking `TimelineState` fields: `camera_rigs`, `cut_track`, `shared_look_at_targets` (serde defaults)
- Cut track with hard cuts and crossfade/blend transitions + easing
- `evaluate_active_camera` with hierarchy transform composition and blend during transitions
- Director monitor compositor: Single / Split H-V / Quad / Picture-in-Picture layouts with on-screen labels
- GLSL `getActiveCamera(float time)` emitter (`glsl-codegen/src/camera`)
- Multi-Cam panel: rig list, cut editing, director monitor, shared targets, active-camera readout
- Tests: `core-engine/tests/phase9_multicam.rs`
### Added
**Phase 8 — Studio-Grade Rendering, Preview & Video Export Pipeline:**
- Offline CPU frame renderer driven by timeline camera evaluation (Shadertoy-resolution presets 640x360 → 1920x1080)
- Live preview panel with hot-reload on timeline revision, split/wipe compare, pixel inspector, histogram & waveform scopes
- Color management: exposure EV, gamma, Reinhard/ACES tone-map, colorblind simulation, `.cube` LUT import with strength blend
- Depth-of-field and motion-blur preview approximations + velocity-vector overlay
- Frame-accurate export job queue (background thread, progress, cancel) writing PNG sequence, BMP sequence, or uncompressed AVI — zero network / no external ffmpeg required at runtime
- Metadata sidecar (`*.meta.txt`) with copyright + version tag
- Core modules: `core-engine/src/color/*`, `core-engine/src/export/*`; app panel `Export / Preview`
- Tests: `core-engine/tests/phase8_export.rs`
### Added
**Phase 7 — Procedural & Expression-Driven Animation Engine:**
- Node-based expression graph IR (`ExpressionGraph` / `NodeKind` / typed sockets) with cycle detection and topological evaluation
- Math, noise (Perlin / Simplex / Worley / FBM), time-driver, channel-reference, and conditional nodes
- Text expression language (recursive-descent parser, AST eval, ternary/compare, safe function set)
- Per-keyframe `expression_override` field on `Keyframe`
- Physically-based secondary motion drivers: spring-damper, camera-shake, overshoot/settle with non-destructive stacking and bake-to-keyframes
- GLSL ES codegen for expression AST + offline noise library (`scpsPerlin2` / `scpsSimplex2` / `scpsWorley2` / `scpsFbm2`) and unsupported-construct diagnostics
- Expressions panel in the app (text override editor, node canvas, driver stack controls)
- Tests: `core-engine/tests/expression_phase7.rs` plus unit tests in expression modules
### Fixed

**Toolchain MSRV mismatch:** bumped `rust-toolchain.toml` from `1.87.0` to `1.89.0` so the workspace builds against current locked dependencies (`wide` 1.5 / `safe_arch` 1.1 require rustc 1.89; `home` 0.5.12, `image` 0.25.10, and `time` 0.3.54 require rustc 1.88+).

notes: All four post-1.0 backlog items, implemented and verified end to end.
## Added
**Drag & drop** — dropping a folder from Windows Explorer onto the Source group sets it as the source directory and prefills the archive name from the folder name.

**Password-protected archives** — an optional "Password-protect" checkbox and password field produce AES-256 encrypted `.zip` files via [SharpZipLib](https://github.com/icsharpcode/SharpZipLib) (`EncryptedArchiveWriter`/`EncryptedArchiveVerifier`), alongside the existing unencrypted Stored/Deflate path.

**Command-line mode** — `ZipAll.exe --source <dir> --dest <dir> [options]` compresses headlessly, sharing the same core engine as the GUI, with `--help`, `--mode`, `--password`, repeatable `--exclude-file`/`--exclude-dir`, and `--quiet`. Running the exe with no arguments (or a single folder path) still opens the GUI.

**Explorer "Send to" integration** — an optional installer task adds a `ZipAll` shortcut to the current user's Send To folder; launching the app with a single folder argument pre-fills that folder as the source in the GUI, so exclusions/password can still be reviewed before compressing.
6 additional unit tests (45 total) covering password round-trips, wrong-password rejection, exclusions, Stored mode, and confirming an unencrypted reader cannot read the encrypted content.
## Verification

Manually verified end-to-end on real Windows hardware: installer rebuilt with the new `sendto` task, install/launch/uninstall cycle (including the Send To shortcut) confirmed clean, Send To launch confirmed via screenshot with the source pre-filled, CLI run from a real console with correct exit codes and output for plain and password-protected archives.
## Known limitations
Tested on Windows 10 x64 only; Windows 11 and ARM64 remain unverified.
ZipAll's first stable release: a native Windows desktop app (C#/.NET, WinForms) that zips a folder, with exclusions, a custom archive name, and a choice of destination.
## Added

`CONTRIBUTING.md`: contribution ground rules (C#/.NET/WinForms-only, English-only, no source comments, White theme only, Windows-only, BCL-only archive format, self-contained-only dependencies), PR checklist, and bug report template.

`tests/ZipAll.Core.Tests`: xUnit unit test project (39 tests) covering `WildcardMatcher`, `ExclusionEngine`, `DirectoryWalker`, and `ArchiveWriter`/`ArchiveVerifier`, including empty folders, deeply nested trees, Unicode/special-character file names, and large flat trees.
`tests/REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md`: manual regression checklist to run against a built installer before every release.
A real application screenshot (`docs/screenshot.png`), now embedded in the README.
## Fixed
Inno Setup script: a mis-escaped `AppId` GUID and a `[Files]` wildcard entry that excluded every file the self-contained publish produces, both of which broke the installer build.

`ArchiveWriter.CreateArchiveAsync` read `ZipArchiveEntry.Length`/`CompressedLength` after writing each entry, but those properties always throw `InvalidOperationException` in `ZipArchiveMode.Create` — every archive containing at least one file was broken. Found while writing the new unit test suite; fixed by deriving byte counts from the known file length and the underlying zip stream's position delta instead.
## Changed
Version stamp moved to `1.0.0` (`MAJOR` now `1`).
Installer build and install/uninstall cycle verified end-to-end (silent install, launch, silent uninstall with no residual files).
Self-contained `win-x86` build published and smoke-tested under WOW64.
## Known limitations
Tested on Windows 10 x64 only; Windows 11 and ARM64 have not been verified (no such machine was available during development).
Zip64 / very large archive support relies on `System.IO.Compression` defaults and has not been explicitly stress-tested with multi-gigabyte archives.
